senses.definition: (literary or poetic) A baby or infant; a very young human or animal. [from 14th c.]
examples: These events came to pass when he was but a babe.

quotes.text:
Though he possess sweet babes and loving wife,
A home of peace by loyal friendships cheered,
And love them more than death or happy life,
quotes.reference: 1874, James Thomson, The City of Dreadful Night:

senses.definition: (slang) An attractive person, especially a young woman. [from 20th c.]

quotes.text: During the 1980s, its vivid streetlife became a symbol of the “consumer socialism” that distinguished Hungary from other Eastern Bloc states, but Budapesters today are rather less enamoured of Váci: dressed-to-kill babes and their sugar daddies would rather pose in malls, and teenagers can find McDonald's anywhere, leaving Váci utterly dependent on tourists for its livelihood and bustle.
quotes.reference: 2002, Charles Hebbert, Dan Richardson, The Rough Guide to Budapest, 2nd edition, London: Rough Guides, →ISBN, page 73:

examples: Hey, babe, how's about you and me getting together?

quotes.text: But, Babe, you don't have to meet 'em if you don't want to.
quotes.reference: 1916 March 11, Charles E. Van Loan, “His Folks”, in Saturday Evening Post:

quotes.text:
But they don't know that your sweet loving, babe
Was here when all my friends were gone
quotes.reference: 1968 December 8, Henry Cosby, Sylvia Moy, Stevie Wonder, “I’d Be a Fool Right Now”, in For Once in My Life, performed by Stevie Wonder, Tamla Records:
